intent.purpose: BE the harness in document form. A single, large, consolidated JSON file that any Claude Code agent loads into context and uses to BEHAVE as if the ideal harness was fully implemented. This means the agent can: make governance decisions (from GOVERNANCE), modify and extend code correctly (from IMPLEMENTATION), assess the current state of all work streams (from STATE), and avoid repeating mistakes (from OPERATIONAL LEARNING). When loaded alongside the rules and CLAUDE.md that CC injects, the agent has the FULL harness.
intent.scope: Everything the harness IS and aspires to be, organized into FOUR PILLARS: GOVERNANCE (what was decided), IMPLEMENTATION (what was built), STATE (where things are), OPERATIONAL LEARNING (what was learned).
intent.audience: Any and all Claude Code agents. Loaded into context at session start.

meta.updateProtocol: Only the commander (Jose) authorizes updates. Agents SURFACE changes as surfacing duty.
meta.staleness: This file is an assumption the moment it is written. Verify claims against live state.
meta.recencyWeight: Produced 2026-03-24 from ALL sources in chronological order. Most recent: running estimate v9.0, OL v3, SQLite RFC. Commander's directive: SQLite migration is the Schwerpunkt.

GOVERNANCE.description: PILLAR 1 -- What was decided. All design principles, rules, frameworks, operative patterns, and decisions that govern agent behavior.

designPrinciples.name: Three-layer governance
designPrinciples.description: Prevention (rules in context stop issues from being created), Detection (hooks fire in real-time during sessions), Audit (skills/subagents provide deep review on demand). Each layer catches what the previous missed.
designPrinciples.evidence: 23 rules (prevention), 11 hooks (detection), /audit skill (audit). All three layers active.
designPrinciples.whatItMeansForYou: When you encounter a governance question, check all three layers: is there a rule? Is there a hook enforcing it? Is there an audit skill that checks it?

designPrinciples.name: Ambiguity is a defect
designPrinciples.description: If a rule, reference, or plan can be read two ways, that is a bug. Surface it immediately via /incident skill.
designPrinciples.evidence: Governed vocabulary (134+ terms), incident governance framework, surfacing duty in hooks.
designPrinciples.whatItMeansForYou: When you read something ambiguous, FILE IT via /incident. Do not interpret silently.

designPrinciples.name: Full context, not token budgeting
designPrinciples.description: Use the full context window. Launch subagents with complete rules. Load reference files generously. Keep CLAUDE.md and rules succinct for clarity, not to save tokens.
designPrinciples.evidence: 1M context window. Commander directive: never let token count influence decisions.
designPrinciples.whatItMeansForYou: Read full files. Include full rules in subagent prompts. Never abbreviate to save tokens.

designPrinciples.name: Specs vs state
designPrinciples.description: Rules and references define what SHOULD be. The /incident skill tracks what IS NOT yet. Never describe a feature as 'working' if it has not fired in production.
designPrinciples.evidence: Incident registry (42+ entries). Planning brief tracks implementation status.
designPrinciples.whatItMeansForYou: Distinguish 'code exists' from 'feature is operational.' Check if code has actually run.

designPrinciples.name: Process discipline as work product
designPrinciples.description: The observation-to-fact pipeline (observe, classify against governed vocabulary, verify against evidence, correct) IS the primary deliverable of every session. Code changes are outputs of the discipline, not substitutes for it.
designPrinciples.evidence: Added to CLAUDE.md as design principle by session 77a33baf (D-v8-6, commit 9faa943).
designPrinciples.whatItMeansForYou: The quality of your process artifacts (running estimate, observations, OL) matters as much as code.

designPrinciples.name: Recency weight
designPrinciples.description: The commander's most recent instruction carries the most weight. Most recently read content has the highest behavioral weight. When instructions conflict in time, the newest wins.
designPrinciples.evidence: Discovered session RnTOD5XJFi. Not yet codified as rule or hook.
designPrinciples.whatItMeansForYou: After loading files, the commander's most recent prompt overrides everything. Re-read it before acting.

designPrinciples.name: Treat static files as assumptions
designPrinciples.description: Everything in files -- including this file -- may be stale. Context (the live conversation) overrides files.
designPrinciples.whatItMeansForYou: Verify file claims against git log, live state, and commander confirmation.

designPrinciples.name: Verify, don't infer
designPrinciples.description: Claims about context state must be verified by reading source files, not inferred from conversation history.
designPrinciples.whatItMeansForYou: Before stating any fact, READ the source. If you cannot read it, mark as ASSUMPTION.

designPrinciples.name: Disciplined initiative (Auftragstaktik)
designPrinciples.description: Mission-type orders with clear boundaries. Initiative within boundaries, escalation when boundaries are unclear.
designPrinciples.whatItMeansForYou: Use judgment within your mission scope. Escalate when scope is unclear. Don't just execute blindly.

designPrinciples.name: Own what matters, rent what doesn't
designPrinciples.description: Build custom for capabilities where ROI justifies it. Rent vendor tools as reference implementation. Own: governance, session lifecycle, context orchestration. Rent: the CC platform, the LLM.
designPrinciples.whatItMeansForYou: When CC doesn't do what we need (e.g., /resume loses framing), build our own (/aitool-resume).

rules.name: Agentic Standards
keyDirectives: All AI CLI invocations use invoke_ai/Invoke-AI from aitools-lib
Speed tiers: fast (haiku), balanced (sonnet), quality (opus)
Permission tiers: none (default), readonly, full, dangerous
Structured prompt pattern: role, context, task, constraints, output format
Every AI invocation logged to deploy.log with telemetry
User-facing AI: show backend+tier+purpose, spinner for >3s, log_error on failure

rules.name: aitools Workspace
keyDirectives: Project-scoped .aitools/ at repo root
User-scoped ~/.aitools/
Cross-machine carry-forward: tracked in git for machine switches
Session-ephemeral data gitignored (scratch, in-flight channels)

rules.name: Artifact Harvesting
keyDirectives: Harvest non-ephemeral from .scratch/ at session end
Must NOT harvest: commit messages, logs, tmp, already-committed files
Auto-prune: >30 days + 0 git refs + not flagged keep + still 'harvested' status
Promote: referenced in git log, manually flagged, or >7 days + similar pattern

rules.name: Config File Write Safety
keyDirectives: Default: read-then-merge for JSON configs
Document managed vs preserved fields in header
Backup before overwrite (backup_file/Backup-File)
Post-write validation: non-empty, valid JSON, required keys
Anti-patterns: cat > EOF for non-sole-owned files, empty catch

rules.name: Cross-Platform Awareness
keyDirectives: Dual-script rule: .sh + .ps1 for every script (exemptions listed)
OS guard patterns: PowerShell checks $IsWindows, bash checks uname -s
Hook portability: uname -s dispatch, NEVER stat -f || stat -c fallback chain
NEVER grep -P (macOS BSD grep doesn't support Perl regex) -- use perl -ne
PowerShell 7 baseline, not PS 5.1
After creating .sh files on Windows: git update-index --chmod=+x

rules.name: Dual Deployment Paths
keyDirectives: Two paths: scripts/ (dev, runtime) and deploy/ (MDM, self-contained)
4 scripts have DUPLICATED logic between scripts/ and build-deploy.sh templates
Template sync: shared/claude-shared.md and dotprofile must stay in sync

rules.name: Documentation Standards
keyDirectives: RELEASE_NOTES format: vX.Y -- Title (date), categorized tables
ROADMAP: In Progress / Planned / Completed tables
Reference doc threshold: >20 lines goes to reference/, not CLAUDE.md
Layered architecture: rules (concise) → references (detail)
@ link convention: resolved in CLAUDE.md, NOT in .claude/rules/

rules.name: Frameworks
keyDirectives: Check before assuming: when encountering a decision with no guidance, invoke /frameworks
Three-layer registry: rule (governance) + JSON (data) + skill (access)
Invoke /frameworks to check coverage, add frameworks, check provenance

rules.name: Git Safety
keyDirectives: deploy/ is ephemeral: 100% generated, reset to HEAD before every pull
scripts/ is source: NEVER bulk-reset
Pre-pull reset scope: ONLY fully generated directories (currently: deploy/)

rules.name: Glossary
keyDirectives: All governed terms listed in the rule (always in context)
Invoke /glossary skill for definitions, new terms, ambiguities
Never read glossary.json directly -- use the skill

rules.name: Governed Data Access
keyDirectives: Governed JSON files accessed ONLY through their governing skill
Rules, CLAUDE.md, references MUST NOT reference JSON file paths
Only skill SKILL.md files and programmatic artifacts may reference JSON paths
Enforcement: pre-commit step 16 (capability bypass audit)

rules.name: Hook Rollout
keyDirectives: Observe-then-enforce cycle: 1+ week observe, review logs, then enforce
Pre-deploy: bash -n syntax check + smoke test (exit 0) + violation test (exit 2)
Per-check mode variables (MODE_AND, MODE_REST, etc.) for granular rollout
Reset to observe after adding new patterns or CC version upgrade

rules.name: Incident Governance
keyDirectives: File via /incident: spec deviations, ambiguities, operational incidents
Severity: critical / high / medium / low
Lifecycle: open → planned → closed
Surfacing duty is CONTINUOUS -- every session actively looks for deficiencies
Ambiguity routing: terminological → /glossary, structural → /incident
Decision tree: spec exists + code deviates → incident; no spec → governance ambiguity

rules.name: Interactive Menus
keyDirectives: Deploy-ManagedFile for interactive diff review
PS1 and bash menus MUST show identical options in identical order
Every return value must be handled at EVERY call site
Non-interactive fallback: AITOOLS_FORCE or non-terminal stdin → overwrite
JSON: field-level review, overwrite/adopt/skip/abort menu

rules.name: Managed File Deployment
keyDirectives: Three types: markdown (diff review), JSON config (read-then-merge), shell script (diff review)
Content sources: dotprofile primary, aitools fallback
Shared requirements: backup, diff logging, post-write validation, three-outcome tracking

rules.name: Plan Execution
keyDirectives: Plans modifying 3+ code files: sub-agent execution pattern
Verbatim code in plan, error-handling audit per block
Fresh sub-agent per batch with rules injected
Main agent verification between batches

rules.name: Script Standards
keyDirectives: Block order (bash): shebang, set -euo pipefail, source aitools-lib + logging_init, OS guard, body, exit footer
Structured logging required: log/log_ok/log_error/log_warn
Error tracking: log_error MUST increment ERRORS, log_warn MUST increment WARNINGS
Exit footer: check ERRORS + WARNINGS counters
External commands: capture output, check exit codes, distinguish up-to-date from failure
write_summary for end-of-run panel (OK/WARN/ERROR/ACTION)
Cross-platform grep: NEVER grep -P, use perl -ne or grep -E

rules.name: Smoke Test Pattern
keyDirectives: Redirect output to log file
Check exit code
Read log only on failure

rules.name: Sources of Truth
keyDirectives: 30+ protected files listed in table
Draft → present for review → wait for approval
Intent statements are protected regardless of file
Exceptions: typos/whitespace, user-dictated exact content

rules.name: Tool Evaluation
keyDirectives: Every managed tool is first-class -- no degraded install methods
8 ranked evaluation principles: official endorsement > provenance > latest stable > cross-platform > same upstream > automation > maintenance > build time
All evaluations through /tool-eval skill

rules.name: Tool Lifecycle
keyDirectives: Phase 2 gate: HARD STOP after install, wait for user approval
Under Evaluation guard: no scripts, no aliases, no build entries until approved
Onboarding checklist: prerequisite eval, non-protected impl, protected review, rebuild+propagate
Install method discovery via /tool-eval (chrome-devtools for official docs)

rules.name: Tool Operations
keyDirectives: Before assuming how a tool behaves, check its ops reference via /tool-ops
Per-tool: deny rules, hooks, context injection, governance modes, verification specs

rules.name: Web Sources
keyDirectives: Chrome DevTools for source-of-truth content (install commands, config steps)
WebFetch for general research, blog posts, quick fact-checks

operativePatterns.name: Demonstrate-then-skip at subsequent transitions
operativePatterns.description: Agent demonstrates correct discipline at first boundary, skips at the next. Urgency overrides discipline.
instanceDetails: Session 77a33baf: pre-commit checklist then straight to execution for D-v8-5
Session RnTOD5XJFi: read files then jumped to editing hooks without plan
S3-Golf: told to read code, demonstrated governance understanding, skipped code
Dashboard: described in prompts but never tested across 3 rounds
operativePatterns.structuralFix: Intent sentinel hook (designed, not deployed). Lagebeurteilung at every execution transition (OL-PR5).
operativePatterns.whatItMeansForYou: You WILL do this. Watch at EVERY transition. When you feel urgency to 'just start doing,' STOP.

operativePatterns.name: Write-on-A, discover-on-B
operativePatterns.description: Code written and tested on one platform, deployed to both, broken on the other.
operativePatterns.structuralFix: check-pre-commit.sh step 17 (IMPLEMENTED). Cross-platform.md hook portability section.
operativePatterns.whatItMeansForYou: ALWAYS use uname -s dispatch for platform-specific commands. NEVER grep -P. Use Perl.

operativePatterns.name: Correct pattern exists but new code uses old pattern
operativePatterns.description: A correct solution exists (get_mtime, uname dispatch) but new code uses the pre-extraction pattern.
operativePatterns.structuralFix: check-pre-commit.sh step 17. This file carries correct patterns forward.
operativePatterns.whatItMeansForYou: Before writing code, check if the harness already has a correct pattern. Check aitools-lib.sh, check-lib.sh, hooks.

operativePatterns.name: 6-stage carry-forward pipeline
operativePatterns.description: Carry-forward is 6 stages: (1) Produce, (2) Commit, (3) Push, (4) Pull, (5) Deploy, (6) Verify. 'Commit and push' addresses only 2 of 6.
operativePatterns.structuralFix: Each stage needs own enforcement. Stage 1: decision #1 auto-commit. Stage 5: hook portability. Stage 6: Lagebeurteilung.
operativePatterns.whatItMeansForYou: Think about ALL 6 stages when producing artifacts that need to carry forward.

operativePatterns.name: Context rot on user intent
operativePatterns.description: After 100K+ tokens of reads, the user's instruction gets buried. Agent executes its own agenda.
operativePatterns.structuralFix: Intent sentinel hook (designed). ~30K batch discipline. Recency weight principle.
operativePatterns.whatItMeansForYou: After 5+ Read calls without user input, STOP and re-read the commander's most recent instruction.

operativePatterns.name: Behavioral framing gap (/resume)
operativePatterns.description: CC /resume preserves text but loses behavioral weight. Content is present but not operative.
operativePatterns.structuralFix: /aitool-resume skill (RFC v7). This harness state file.
operativePatterns.whatItMeansForYou: If in a /resume session, read OL and this file FRESH from disk to restore behavioral framing.

operativePatterns.name: Assumption propagation (chain-of-trust failure)
operativePatterns.description: Agent states assumption as fact. Downstream agents trust without verifying. Propagates through artifacts.
operativePatterns.structuralFix: Delegation duty assumption injection (proposed). Verification pattern (proposed).
operativePatterns.whatItMeansForYou: Before stating a fact, VERIFY by reading the source. If you cannot read, mark as ASSUMPTION.

operativePatterns.name: UCIs are ineffective for recurring patterns
operativePatterns.description: Behavioral coaching items fade over time. For 3+ occurrences, only structural fixes (hooks) work.
operativePatterns.structuralFix: Hooks for recurring patterns. Intent sentinel for context rot. Step 17 for platform portability.
operativePatterns.whatItMeansForYou: Do NOT propose UCIs for recurring problems. Propose hooks, skills, rules -- structural enforcement.

IMPLEMENTATION.description: PILLAR 2 -- What was built. Every hook, key scripts, dashboard system, deploy pipeline, code patterns. An agent reading this can modify any component correctly.

hooks.description: 11 hooks form the detection layer. Three event types: SessionStart (2), SessionEnd (3), Stop (2), PreToolUse (3), PostToolUse (1).

hooks.name: block-claude-code-guide.sh
hooks.whatItDoes: Blocks the built-in Haiku-based claude-code-guide subagent that returns inaccurate schema information (caused incident #34730 where all hooks were disabled). Returns JSON deny with corrective context: hook type schemas, official doc URLs at code.claude.com.
hooks.behavioralImpact: Agent receives corrective context about hook schemas and documentation sources instead of inaccurate Haiku output. Prevents cascade failure from bad schema info.
hooks.outputMechanism: stdout JSON with permissionDecision:deny and permissionDecisionReason containing corrective context
hooks.portability: All platforms (pure bash regex, no platform-specific commands)

hooks.name: dashboard-serve.sh
hooks.whatItDoes: Thin dispatcher to 'aitools dashboard --background'. Extracts project root from hook input JSON. Finds aitools CLI (command -v or ~/.local/bin/). Falls back to direct Python launch if CLI not installed. Auto-detects running estimate from .aitools/channel/ then .scratch/. Default port 8411.
hooks.behavioralImpact: Dashboard auto-launches at session start. Agent sees 'Dashboard: http://localhost:PORT/' in context.

hooks.name: estimate-refresh-stop.sh
hooks.whatItDoes: Two functions: (1) Increments turn count in /tmp/aitools-estimate-$session_id/turn-count. (2) At turn 15 and every 15 turns: injects Lagebeurteilung reminder listing key fields to refresh. Every 10 turns after turn 5: checks running estimate file mtime, warns if >30 min stale. Uses uname -s dispatch for stat (fixed commit 2175814).
hooks.behavioralImpact: Agent gets periodic reminders to update running estimate. Triggers dashboard auto-refresh cycle.

hooks.name: glossary-skill-guard.sh
hooks.eventTrigger: Read or Grep of glossary.json or glossary.md
hooks.whatItDoes: Detects direct access to glossary files. Reminds agent to use /glossary skill instead. Always exits 0 (advisory). Uses Perl for JSON parsing.
hooks.behavioralImpact: Agent reminded to use governed access pattern.

hooks.name: harvest-session.sh
hooks.whatItDoes: Classifies scratch contents by extension. Ephemeral (logs, tmp, commit-msg) skipped. Non-ephemeral copied to harvesting/ with YYYY-MM-DD_session-PREFIX_filename. Handoff files routed to .aitools/channel/handoffs/. Auto-creates harvesting/ and harvest-manifest.json on first harvest. Updates manifest via node. Audit: marks stale artifacts (>pruneAfter, 0 git refs) as pruned. Reports results to stderr. Does NOT delete session dir (30-file loss lesson). Does NOT do git ops (decision #1 not implemented).
hooks.behavioralImpact: Session artifacts are preserved in harvesting/ for later review and promotion.

hooks.name: scratch-init.sh
hooks.whatItDoes: Creates .scratch/session-{first 10 chars of session_id}/ directory. Fallback to mktemp if no session_id. Logs stale session dirs (>24h) but does NOT auto-delete. Discovers handoffs at .aitools/channel/handoffs/ and announces them. Writes .scratch/.current-session pointer.
hooks.behavioralImpact: Agent gets scratch directory path and handoff announcements in context.

hooks.name: session-archive.sh
hooks.whatItDoes: Copies transcript JSONL to dotprofile repo at sessions/{project}/{date}_{prefix}.jsonl. Reads userRepoPath from ~/.aitools/config.json. Derives project from git root. Uses transcript birth time for date (uname -s dispatch for stat). No git ops.
hooks.behavioralImpact: Session transcripts archived for future reference and /aitool-resume.

hooks.name: sh-file-fixup.sh
hooks.eventTrigger: After Write or Edit of any .sh file
hooks.whatItDoes: Auto-fixes: CRLF → LF (Perl), chmod +x on disk, git update-index --chmod=+x if tracked with wrong mode. Reports fixes to stderr.
hooks.behavioralImpact: Eliminates manual .sh file fixup cycle. Agent sees fixup report.

hooks.name: standing-order-guard.sh
hooks.whatItDoes: Enforces 3 USOs: (1) Dedicated tools -- blocks cat/head/tail/grep/find/sed/awk as first token (pipeline-exempt). (2) Scratch files -- blocks commands with 5+ lines (4+ escaped newlines). (3) Simple Bash -- blocks && (ENFORCE), || (observe), ; (observe, exempt pwsh/perl), $() (ENFORCE), backticks (observe), globs in rm. Per-check mode variables. Pure-bash JSON parsing. Logs to ~/.claude/hooks/logs/standing-order-guard.log.
hooks.behavioralImpact: Prevents agents from using Bash for file ops (redirects to Read/Write/Edit/Grep/Glob), from inlining complex scripts, and from using compound operators.
hooks.outputMechanism: stderr for block messages (shown to agent). Exit 2 = block. Exit 0 = allow.

enforcementState.MODE_REST_OR_PIPE_SEMI_BACKTICK: observe (false positives exist or low sample)

hooks.name: surfacing-duty-stop.sh
hooks.whatItDoes: Two functions: (1) Periodic reminder every 30 minutes to check for incidents/ambiguities. Uses marker file in /tmp/aitools-surfacing-$session_id/. (2) Incident-acknowledgment detection: scans last 100 lines of transcript for phrases like 'pre-existing incident', 'known gap' without /incident invocation or TODO(incident): marker. Suppresses if incidents.json modified in last 30 min. Uses uname -s dispatch for stat.
hooks.behavioralImpact: Agent reminded of surfacing duty. Caught when acknowledging incidents without filing.

hooks.name: tool-ops-session-audit.sh
hooks.whatItDoes: Contract tests: (1) Tests block-claude-code-guide.sh correctly denies claude-code-guide and allows Explore. (2) Drift detection: checks hook is registered in settings.json. (3) Staleness: counts CRITICAL items in tool-ops-claude-code.md. Logs to ~/.claude/hooks/logs/tool-ops-audit.jsonl.
hooks.behavioralImpact: Automated verification of deployed hook behavior at every session end.

dashboardSystem.description: Three-component live dashboard system. Fully shipped and verified working 2026-03-24.

generator.purpose: Reads running estimate JSON, produces self-contained HTML dashboard

modes.static: Default. Embeds JSON into HTML. Works from file:///.
modes.live: --serve flag. Starts HTTP server with file watcher. Dashboard polls /api/estimate every 3 seconds. Re-renders without page reload.

generator.dataFlow: running-estimate.json → load_estimate() → build_html() → write HTML. In live mode: HTTPServer serves HTML + /api/estimate endpoint, FileWatcher thread checks mtime, regenerates on change.
generator.sections: Header, summary stats, schwerpunkt, phase tracker, decisions, findings, observations, assumptions, delegation log
generator.dependencies: Python stdlib only (http.server, json, threading, pathlib)

hook.purpose: SessionStart thin dispatcher to aitools dashboard --background
hook.fallback: Direct Python launch if CLI not installed

dashboardSystem.dataFlow: Agent updates estimate JSON → file mtime changes → server FileWatcher detects → regenerates HTML → browser polls /api/estimate → re-renders
dashboardSystem.knownLimitation: Single PID file (.aitools/.dashboard-pid) blocks multiple instances via shell wrapper. Use python3 generate-dashboard.py directly for multi-port.

deployPipeline.description: Source → build → deploy. Two paths that must produce equivalent results.
deployPipeline.devPath: scripts/ → runtime execution by aitools CLI. Source of truth.
deployPipeline.mdmPath: deploy/ → generated by build-deploy.sh. Self-contained. Reset to HEAD before every pull.
deployPipeline.buildProcess: build-deploy.sh reads scripts/ + shared/ at build time, inlines aitools-lib into deploy scripts, embeds shared content (hooks, skills, templates). deploy/ has no runtime dependency on the repo.
knownFragilities: 4 scripts with duplicated logic between scripts/ and build-deploy.sh templates (setup-user-claude, setup-user-cursor, setup-user-mcp, setup-user-hooks)
Deploy-Configs in aitools.ps1 uses *> $null 2>> $logFile -- silent failure pattern
deploy/ is ephemeral -- uncommitted changes lost on every aitools sync

scriptInventory.setupScripts: 13 tool pairs (setup-{tool}.sh + .ps1): datadog, gh-cli, go, modal, pandoc, perl, python, rust, typst, uv, vercelcli + user-claude, user-cursor, user-hooks, user-mcp, user-skills, cursor-ide-mcp

correct.example: if [ "$(uname -s)" = "Darwin" ]; then stat -f %m; else stat -c %Y; fi
json_field() with bash regex or grep+sed

correct.pattern: Perl for CRLF and string manipulation

antiPatterns.why: GNU stat -f means --file-system. Partially succeeds with multiline output. Under set -u, crashes. Recurred 4 times.
Not available on macOS BSD grep

antiPatterns.pattern: Long inline commands in Bash tool
antiPatterns.why: Triggers standing-order-guard hook. Hard to review.
Silently swallows errors, including parse failures
Use Write tool for file creation

antiPatterns.pattern: $() or backticks in Bash tool calls
antiPatterns.fix: Compute in prior step, write to temp file

OPERATIONAL_LEARNING.description: PILLAR 4 -- What was learned. Institutional memory with patterns, proposals, carry-forward gaps, and meta-lessons.

observations.text: Carry-forward pipeline structural gap: SessionEnd outputs produced but never committed. Every session without decision #1 loses artifacts.
Cross-platform hook failures are recurring (4th instance). All written on macOS, tested on macOS, discovered broken on Windows.
Correct patterns exist (get_mtime, uname dispatch) but new code uses old broken patterns.
Governed vocabulary enforces observation precision. 3 passes caught errors each time.
Search breadth determines discovery quality. 1 term: 0 results. 30 terms: 64+ commits.
Platform transitions require Lagebeurteilung before resuming prior Schwerpunkt.
Deploy-Configs suppresses all output (*> $null). 6 scripts crashed with zero diagnostic output.
Agent demonstrated correct discipline then skipped it at the next transition. Commander caught: 'stop for a second.'
Subagents cannot Glob/Grep outside current repo. CAN Read with explicit absolute paths.

insights.text: Commit gap: SessionEnd outputs never committed. Decision #1 is the designed fix -- not implemented across 6 sessions.
No detection layer existed for platform portability. Now: check-pre-commit step 17.
Governed vocabulary is an active quality gate, not documentation.
Need configuration audit for cross-machine state (ISO 10007).
Carry-forward is a 6-stage pipeline. 'Commit and push' is 2 of 6.
Carry-forward is session-to-session, not machine-to-machine. Bidirectional merge.

patterns.name: Correct pattern exists but new code uses old
6-stage carry-forward pipeline

architecture.tier1: Per-session DBs at .aitools/sessions/<id>.db. WAL mode. Written by that session's agents only.
architecture.tier2: Harness DB at .aitools/harness.db. Cross-session state. Updated at session boundaries.
architecture.jsonArchive: Tracked in git. JSON exports committed at session end. Carries forward via git pull.
architecture.accessMethod: Python sqlite3 only. No sqlite3 CLI dependency (unavailable on Windows Git Bash).
architecture.hookPerformance: Stop hooks use file mtime (~1ms). SessionStart/End hooks can afford Python subprocess (~100-200ms).

migrationPhases: Phase 2: Migrate hooks (SessionStart creates DB, SessionEnd exports JSON)
Phase 3: Migrate dashboard (read from DB instead of JSON)
sqliteMigration.commanderDirective: Everything goes into the DB -- not just running estimate. Multi-DB, not single. Migration NOW.

metaLessons.description: 29 hard-won operational learning items. Not suggestions -- structural observations about how agents fail.
items: Recency weight: most recent instruction wins
Static files are assumptions -- verify against live state
Verify, don't infer -- read source files, don't trust history
Disciplined initiative -- surface ambiguity rather than assuming
Never use Explore agents -- always general-purpose with write permissions
UCIs are ineffective -- only structural fixes (hooks, scripts, rules) work for recurring patterns
~30K batch discipline -- re-read mission objective after 5+ Reads
Demonstrate-then-skip (4 occurrences) -- watch every transition boundary
Context rot on user intent -- after 100K+ tokens, objective gets buried
Behavioral framing gap -- presence is not behavioral weight
Write-on-A, discover-on-B (5 instances) -- uname -s dispatch, Perl not grep -P
Assumption propagation -- verify every fact, mark unverifiable as ASSUMPTION
The file you produce IS the harness -- every word has behavioral consequences
Human-readable labels -- always include labels alongside IDs
6-stage carry-forward pipeline -- each stage fails independently
Subagent access barrier -- cannot Glob/Grep outside repo, CAN Read with absolute paths
Subagent blank slate -- inherit NOTHING, every delegation includes full context
1M context -- never 'too large', read full files, no token-based decisions
Parallel execution -- launch independent tasks in parallel
Re-read before acting -- the commander's most repeated instruction
Audit shipped capabilities -- check CODE not just DECISIONS
Artifact includes implementation -- harness IS code + governance + state + OL
Dashboard miss meta-lesson -- 3 rounds missed shipped code because code was invisible to governance analysts
Skeleton is incomplete -- missing implementation and OL pillars
Multi-turn self-audit -- after reading audit, after drafting audit against all context
Worktrees disproved -- gitignored files absent, untracked files absent
Dashboard multi-port PID limitation -- use python3 directly, not shell wrapper
SendMessage unavailable -- gated behind Agent Teams flag
SQLite migration is Schwerpunkt -- everything into DB, multi-DB, Python sqlite3
